neighbours.label: A determiner or possessive where a body part is expected next (under the skin, until your knees, retract their claws)
fire: The nurse gave the shot just under the skin.
The wrestler stood tall, with his arms raised.
Dogs often lick their paws after a walk.
Keep going down until your knees are bent.
She has a small scar under her chin.
He stood there and crossed his arms.
Birds use their beaks to open seeds.
The patient raised her hand and closed her eyes.
quiet: The nurse put the note just under the door.
The winner stood tall, holding the trophy high.
Dogs often chew their toys after a walk.
Keep going down until you reach the lake.
She has a small shed behind her house.
He stood there and read his mail.
Birds use their nests to raise chicks.
The patient paid her bill and called her sister.

predictions: The determiner before a body part fires. Determiners before other nouns stay quiet, when the lead-in gives no expectation of a body part.
